records.context: The window is frameless and the menu bar is what you drag it by. Its first backing store is filled with the splash colour so the compositor cannot expose stale desktop pixels before anything has drawn -- deliberately without ``WA_OpaquePaintEvent``, which is a promise to paint every pixel that this window cannot keep once the application stylesheet clears ``autoFillBackground`` again. records.context: ``QThread.terminate()`` is ``pthread_cancel`` under the covers, and every independent execution path in this application executes Python. A cancelled independent execution path that happened to hold the GIL never releases it and the whole process stops making progress; one cancelled inside a Qt or PySide internal leaves a corrupt heap and the process dies later, somewhere unrelated. Neither failure names the line that caused it, which is why :meth:`RunRegistry.cancel_all` documents "refuse to destroy the GUI rather than use ``QThread.terminate()``" — this function is how a caller does that.

records.source: ``QThread.terminate()`` is ``pthread_cancel`` under the covers, and every thread in this application runs Python. A cancelled thread that happened to hold the GIL never releases it and the whole process stops making progress; one cancelled inside a Qt or PySide internal leaves a corrupt heap and the process dies later, somewhere unrelated. Neither failure names the line that caused it, which is why :meth:`RunRegistry.cancel_all` documents "refuse to destroy the GUI rather than use ``QThread.terminate()``" — this function is how a caller does that.
records.translation: ``QThread.terminate()`` भीतर से ``pthread_cancel`` है, और इस एप्लिकेशन का हर थ्रेड Python चलाता है। GIL पकड़े हुए रद्द किया गया थ्रेड उसे कभी नहीं छोड़ता और पूरी प्रक्रिया आगे बढ़ना बंद कर देती है; Qt या PySide के भीतर रद्द किया गया थ्रेड दूषित heap छोड़ता है और प्रक्रिया बाद में किसी असंबंधित जगह मर जाती है। कोई भी विफलता उस पंक्ति का नाम नहीं बताती जिसने उसे उत्पन्न किया, इसी कारण :meth:`RunRegistry.cancel_all` दर्ज करता है "``QThread.terminate()`` का उपयोग करने के बजाय GUI को नष्ट करने से मना करें" — और यह फ़ंक्शन वह तरीका है जिससे कॉलर ऐसा करता है।

records.context: The application's ``aboutToQuit`` drain and the interpreter's exit hook both end here. ``aboutToQuit`` only fires when an event loop quits, so a process that builds windows and then simply ends (a script, a test subprocess, a capture run that returns early) never sees it, and the QThreads its widgets started are destroyed during interpreter teardown while they still run. records.context: The two differ in exactly one place, and it matters only there. A block registered with :func:`register_widget_qss` is handed the ``opacity`` :func:`stylesheet` was called with, and that is ``None`` when the caller asked for the theme's *designed* scrim rather than any user's setting — the documented meaning of ``surface_opacity=None``, and what every built-in rule in this file honours through :func:`panel_alpha`.
records.label: spacr.qt.theme.block_surface#1

records.source: The two differ in exactly one place, and it matters only there. A block registered with :func:`register_widget_qss` is handed the ``opacity`` :func:`stylesheet` was called with, and that is ``None`` when the caller asked for the theme's *designed* scrim rather than any user's setting — the documented meaning of ``surface_opacity=None``, and what every built-in rule in this file honours through :func:`panel_alpha`.
records.translation: दोनों में ठीक एक जगह अंतर है, और वह केवल वहीं मायने रखता है। :func:`register_widget_qss` से पंजीकृत block को वही ``opacity`` दी जाती है जिसके साथ :func:`stylesheet` कॉल हुआ था, और वह ``None`` होती है जब कॉलर ने किसी उपयोगकर्ता की सेटिंग के बजाय थीम का *designed* (डिज़ाइन किया गया) scrim माँगा — यही ``surface_opacity=None`` का प्रलेखित अर्थ है, और इस फ़ाइल का हर built-in नियम :func:`panel_alpha` के माध्यम से इसका पालन करता है।

records.context: :func:`pane_surface` cannot honour it. Its ``None`` means "nobody told me, go and look", so it reads the live page-opacity preference. That is right for the inline and paint-time callers it was written for — Home's aside panels have no ``stylesheet`` argument to plumb through — and wrong inside a block, where ``None`` was already an answer. The consequence was that ``stylesheet("dark")`` emitted ``rgba(22, 23, 25, 0.600)`` for every block that passed it through: a function of its arguments quietly depending on a QSettings value, which made the assertion that the opaque themes emit plain hex pass or fail on module import order.

That is right for the inline and paint-time callers it was written for — Home's aside panels have no ``stylesheet`` argument to plumb through — and wrong inside a block, where ``None`` was already an answer. The consequence was that ``stylesheet("dark")`` emitted ``rgba(22, 23, 25, 0.600)`` for every block that passed it through: a function of its arguments quietly depending on a QSettings value, which made the assertion that the opaque themes emit plain hex pass or fail on module import order.
records.translation: :func:`pane_surface` इसका पालन नहीं कर सकता। उसके ``None`` का अर्थ है "किसी ने नहीं बताया, जाकर देखो", इसलिए वह live page-opacity वरीयता पढ़ता है। जिन inline और paint-time कॉलरों के लिए वह लिखा गया था उनके लिए यह सही है — Home के aside पैनलों के पास आगे भेजने के लिए कोई ``stylesheet`` तर्क नहीं है — और block के भीतर गलत है, जहाँ ``None`` पहले से एक उत्तर था। परिणाम यह था कि ``stylesheet("dark")`` उसे आगे भेजने वाले हर block के लिए ``rgba(22, 23, 25, 0.600)`` देता था: अपने तर्कों का एक फ़ंक्शन चुपचाप एक QSettings मान पर निर्भर था, जिसके कारण यह assertion कि अपारदर्शी थीमें साधारण hex देती हैं, module import क्रम के अनुसार पास या फ़ेल होता था।

records.context: Most spaCR application views are plain ``QWidget`` trees. A ``QWidget`` with no QSS rule of its own inherits the blanket ``QWidget {{ background-color: bg }}`` and paints the WINDOW colour — which is not a surface, so no value of the page-opacity preference can reach it. That is why an application view could sit as a black slab over the animated background no matter what the slider said.
records.label: spacr.qt.theme.clear_container_surfaces#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Most spaCR screens are plain ``QWidget`` trees. A ``QWidget`` with no QSS rule of its own inherits the blanket ``QWidget {{ background-color: bg }}`` and paints the WINDOW colour — which is not a surface, so no value of the page-opacity preference can reach it. That is why a screen could sit as a black slab over the animated background no matter what the slider said.
records.translation: अधिकांश spaCR स्क्रीनें साधारण ``QWidget`` trees हैं। जिस ``QWidget`` का अपना कोई QSS नियम नहीं होता, वह व्यापक ``QWidget {{ background-color: bg }}`` नियम विरासत में लेता है और विंडो (WINDOW) का रंग चित्रित करता है — जो surface नहीं है, इसलिए page-opacity वरीयता का कोई भी मान उस तक नहीं पहुँच सकता। इसी कारण slider चाहे जो कहे, स्क्रीन animated पृष्ठभूमि के ऊपर एक काली पट्टी की तरह दिख सकती थी।

records.source: A backdrop — the theme's wallpaper, or the DNA rain on the sequencing screen — is behind the *page*, and in the opaque themes every container between it and the eye is an opaque ``bg`` by virtue of the blanket ``QWidget`` rule. One container is enough to bury it: a screen's header widget, its splitter, a scroll area and that scroll area's viewport are each a QWidget, and each one used to paint solid black over the animation the screen had just installed.
records.translation: पृष्ठभूमि — थीम का wallpaper, या sequencing स्क्रीन पर DNA rain — *पृष्ठ* के पीछे होती है, और अपारदर्शी थीमों में उसके और आँख के बीच का हर container एक अपारदर्शी ``bg`` होता है, जिसका कारण व्यापक ``QWidget`` नियम है। उसे ढकने के लिए एक container पर्याप्त है: स्क्रीन का header विजेट, उसका splitter, एक scroll area और उस scroll area का viewport, हर एक QWidget है, और हर एक पहले उसी animation के ऊपर ठोस काला रंग चित्रित करता था जिसे स्क्रीन ने अभी-अभी स्थापित किया था।

records.context: Tag the layout containers with this and the backdrop reaches the eye; leave the cards, panels and inputs alone and they stay the readable surface on top of it. Safe to call on a widget that is already visible — the style is re-polished so the change takes effect immediately rather than at the next theme switch. A widget no stylesheet reaches yet, or one in a window whose sheet is held (:func:`_one_sheet_for`), is only tagged: nothing reads the tag until a sheet arrives, and putting a sheet on polishes every widget it reaches. Glassing Preferences tags about 400 containers, and polishing each one before its sheet went on cost 53-64 ms for nothing.

records.source: Two screens said this before the mechanism existed, by giving the view an object name and registering a whole QSS block for it — Model Compare's result tables, Model Zoo's listing and provenance box. An ID selector outranks the transparent tag the same way. This is that without the block: one call, and either the shipped table rule or the ``*[spacrSurface="true"]`` rule supplies the fill at the user's page opacity. The second is not redundant: nothing in the sheet covers a bare ``QListWidget``, which would otherwise fall through to the blanket ``QWidget`` rule and paint the WINDOW colour, which is not a surface.
records.translation: इस तंत्र के अस्तित्व से पहले दो स्क्रीनों ने यह बात view को object name देकर और उसके लिए पूरा QSS block पंजीकृत करके कही थी — Model Compare की परिणाम तालिकाएँ, Model Zoo की सूची और provenance बॉक्स। ID selector भी उसी तरह transparent चिह्न से अधिक प्राथमिकता रखता है। यह वही है, बिना block के: एक कॉल, और या तो दिया गया table नियम या ``*[spacrSurface="true"]`` नियम उपयोगकर्ता की page opacity पर भराव देता है। दूसरा अनावश्यक नहीं है: sheet में कुछ भी साधारण ``QListWidget`` को कवर नहीं करता, जो अन्यथा व्यापक ``QWidget`` नियम तक पहुँचकर विंडो (WINDOW) का रंग चित्रित करेगा, जो surface नहीं है।

records.source: Safe to call before or after the sweep, and safe to call twice: the transparent tag is cleared as well as the surface tag set, and the style is re-polished so a visible widget changes immediately.
records.translation: sweep से पहले या बाद में कॉल करना सुरक्षित है, और दो बार कॉल करना भी सुरक्षित है: surface चिह्न लगाने के साथ transparent चिह्न हटाया भी जाता है, और style फिर से polish की जाती है ताकि दिख रहा विजेट तुरंत बदले।

records.context: One Qt rule has to be paid on the way. A **subclass** of ``QWidget`` ignores a QSS background entirely unless ``WA_StyledBackground`` is set, which is why Power's caveat panel still measured the backdrop untouched with a matching rule sitting in the sheet. The attribute is set here for those, and deliberately NOT for a ``QAbstractScrollArea``: a view already paints its background through its viewport, and a second styled fill on top of that is the two-surfaces-stacked fault again. Measured both ways rather than reasoned about.

records.source: One Qt rule has to be paid on the way. A **subclass** of ``QWidget`` ignores a QSS background entirely unless ``WA_StyledBackground`` is set, which is why Power's caveat panel still measured the backdrop untouched with a matching rule sitting in the sheet. The attribute is set here for those, and deliberately NOT for a ``QAbstractScrollArea``: a view already paints its background through its viewport, and a second styled fill on top of that is the two-surfaces-stacked fault again. Measured both ways rather than reasoned about.
records.translation: रास्ते में Qt के एक नियम का पालन करना पड़ता है। ``QWidget`` का **subclass** QSS पृष्ठभूमि को पूरी तरह अनदेखा करता है जब तक ``WA_StyledBackground`` सेट न हो, इसी कारण sheet में मेल खाता नियम होने पर भी Power के caveat पैनल पर पृष्ठभूमि बिना बदले मापी गई। उनके लिए यह attribute यहाँ सेट किया जाता है, और जानबूझकर ``QAbstractScrollArea`` के लिए नहीं (NOT): view अपनी पृष्ठभूमि पहले से अपने viewport के माध्यम से चित्रित करता है, और उसके ऊपर दूसरा styled भराव फिर से दो surfaces के एक के ऊपर एक होने वाली गलती है। यह तर्क से नहीं, दोनों तरह से मापकर तय किया गया।

records.source: **Cell** wallpapers always come out of :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.render`, which exposure-solves every frame it returns — the shipped masters and the user's own drop-in alike. records.translation: **Cell** wallpapers हमेशा :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.render` से आते हैं, जो अपने लौटाए हर frame का exposure हल करता है — दिए गए masters और उपयोगकर्ता की अपनी drop-in छवियाँ, दोनों का। इसलिए Cell पृष्ठभूमि का कोई भी पाठ-पंक्ति आकार का क्षेत्र :func:`max_background_luma` से अधिक नहीं हो सकता, और Cell पैनल को जिस सबसे खराब स्थिति को झेलना है वह सफ़ेद नहीं, यही सीमा है। मापा गया: दिया गया ``microtubules`` master 0.109 की सीमा के सामने 0.098 के शिखर पर है, ``filopodia`` 0.073 पर।

Only a strong scrim saves text over that, so Space is judged against white and its panels stay much more opaque than Cell's.

records.context: For a widget that is a sheet root. Before per-application view sheeting, a module application view's own stylesheet held only its own rules and the APPLICATION carried the theme, so `setStyleSheet` on the application view was a safe, local thing to do. records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: FOR A WIDGET THAT IS A SHEET ROOT. Before per-screen sheeting, a module screen's own stylesheet held only its own rules and the APPLICATION carried the theme, so `setStyleSheet` on the screen was a safe, local thing to do. Now the screen may be carrying all ~73 KB of the window sheet, and a plain `setStyleSheet` throws the theme away.
records.translation: ऐसे विजेट के लिए जो sheet root है (FOR A WIDGET THAT IS A SHEET ROOT)। प्रति-स्क्रीन sheeting से पहले, module स्क्रीन की अपनी stylesheet में केवल उसके अपने नियम होते थे और थीम एप्लिकेशन (APPLICATION) धारण करता था, इसलिए स्क्रीन पर `setStyleSheet` एक सुरक्षित, स्थानीय क्रिया थी। अब स्क्रीन विंडो sheet का पूरा ~73 KB धारण कर रही हो सकती है, और साधारण `setStyleSheet` थीम को फेंक देता है।

records.context: :mod:`spacr.cell_montage` selects the objects and records the selection reason; this module resolves and displays their extracted image regions beside the processing session's figures. Each attached database resolves its own exported-PNG or ``merged/<fov>.npy`` source so multi-plate montages can combine experiments with different storage layouts. The extracted image region mask image layer and image data channels come from :class:`spacr.crops.CropSpec` or, by default, the processing session's ``measurements.db`` metadata.

records.source: :mod:`spacr.cell_montage` selects the objects and records the selection reason; this module resolves and displays their image crops beside the run's figures. Each attached database resolves its own exported-PNG or ``merged/<fov>.npy`` source so multi-plate montages can combine experiments with different storage layouts. The crop mask plane and channels come from :class:`spacr.crops.CropSpec` or, by default, the run's ``measurements.db`` metadata.
records.translation: :mod:`spacr.cell_montage` objects चुनता है और चयन का कारण दर्ज करता है; यह मॉड्यूल उनके image crops निर्धारित करता है और उन्हें रन के figures के पास दिखाता है। हर जुड़ा डेटाबेस अपना exported-PNG या ``merged/<fov>.npy`` source स्वयं निर्धारित करता है, ताकि multi-plate montages अलग-अलग storage विन्यास वाले प्रयोगों को जोड़ सकें। crop mask plane और channels :class:`spacr.crops.CropSpec` से आते हैं, या डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से रन के ``measurements.db`` metadata से।

records.source: **Cheap on open.** ``PRAGMA table_info`` is free; ``SELECT COUNT(*)`` over a 400 k-row measurement table is not. Opening the dialog runs no count at all. The per-table row figure comes from ``max(_rowid_)`` and is labelled an estimate; a per-column non-null count happens only when the user asks for it by name. records.translation: **खुलने पर सस्ता।** ``PRAGMA table_info`` मुफ़्त है; 400 k-पंक्ति measurement तालिका पर ``SELECT COUNT(*)`` नहीं। dialog खोलने पर कोई गिनती नहीं चलती। प्रति-तालिका पंक्ति संख्या ``max(_rowid_)`` से आती है और उसे अनुमान बताया जाता है; प्रति-कॉलम non-null गिनती केवल तब होती है जब उपयोगकर्ता उसे नाम लेकर माँगे। (``_rowid_``, ``rowid`` नहीं — देखें :meth:`SchemaReader.estimate_rows`, जहाँ अंतर एक पूर्ण table scan और उसके बाद ``ValueError`` का था।)

records.context: **Background loading.** The picker does not freeze the GUI. It performs four sequential sqlite queries: open, list tables, read one table's columns, and estimate its rows. Previously, before a dialog appeared, all four queries ran in ``__init__``. Cold measurements were 45 ms for measurements.db, a 383 MB database, and 87 ms for a schema with 1 500 tables. The dialog now selects background mode with ``threaded=True``. All reads are performed by :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. Synchronous mode remains the initial choice; :class:`ColumnPickerDialog` explains why.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.column_picker#9

records.source: **Off the GUI thread.** Cheap is not free, and opening the picker is four sequential sqlite round trips — open, list tables, read one table's columns, estimate its rows — every one of which used to happen inside ``__init__``, before the modal appeared. Measured cold on a 383 MB measurements.db that is 45 ms, and on a 1 500-table schema 87 ms, entirely between the click and any window. The button now builds the dialog with ``threaded=True`` and the reads arrive from a :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. The default is still the synchronous mode, deliberately; :class:`ColumnPickerDialog` says why.
records.translation: **GUI थ्रेड से बाहर।** सस्ता होना मुफ़्त होना नहीं है, और picker खोलना चार क्रमिक sqlite round trips है — खोलना, तालिकाओं की सूची, एक तालिका के कॉलम पढ़ना, उसकी पंक्तियों का अनुमान — और ये सभी पहले ``__init__`` के भीतर, modal दिखने से पहले होते थे। 383 MB measurements.db पर cold मापने पर यह 45 ms है, और 1 500-तालिका schema पर 87 ms, पूरी तरह क्लिक और किसी भी विंडो के बीच। बटन अब dialog को ``threaded=True`` के साथ बनाता है और reads एक :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner` से आते हैं। डिफ़ॉल्ट अब भी जानबूझकर synchronous मोड है; :class:`ColumnPickerDialog` कारण बताता है।

records.context: ``threaded=False`` (the default) reads the schema inside ``__init__``: when the constructor returns, the tables are listed, a table is selected, its columns are in the tree and the name box has been judged. That is what every programmatic caller and the ~60 tests in ``tests/qt/test_column_picker.py`` are written against — they construct a dialog and assert on its contents on the next line, with no event loop anywhere (the suite's autouse fixture makes ``QDialog.exec`` raise). Defaulting to the asynchronous mode would turn every one of those into a race, so it is opt-in.

records.source: ``threaded=False`` (the default) reads the schema inside ``__init__``: when the constructor returns, the tables are listed, a table is selected, its columns are in the tree and the name box has been judged. records.translation: ``threaded=False`` (डिफ़ॉल्ट) schema को ``__init__`` के भीतर पढ़ता है: constructor के लौटने तक तालिकाएँ सूचीबद्ध होती हैं, एक तालिका चुनी जाती है, उसके कॉलम tree में होते हैं और नाम बॉक्स का मूल्यांकन हो चुका होता है। हर programmatic कॉलर और ``tests/qt/test_column_picker.py`` के ~60 परीक्षण इसी के अनुसार लिखे गए हैं — वे dialog बनाते हैं और अगली ही पंक्ति में उसकी सामग्री पर assert करते हैं, कहीं भी कोई event loop नहीं (suite का autouse fixture ``QDialog.exec`` को अपवाद उठाने वाला बना देता है)। asynchronous मोड को डिफ़ॉल्ट बनाने से इनमें से हर एक race बन जाएगा, इसलिए वह opt-in है।

records.context: ``threaded=True`` is what the ``SQL`` button uses (:meth:`ColumnPickerButton.make_dialog`), and it is the real user-facing path. The window appears immediately saying it is reading the schema, and the tables, columns and row estimate arrive from a :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. That matters because opening the picker is four sequential sqlite round trips against a file that is usually cold and often on a network mount — measured at 45 ms on a 383 MB measurements.db with nothing cached and 87 ms on a 1 500-table schema, all of it dead time between the click and the window.

records.context: It is spelt ``_rowid_`` for a reason. Every spaCR object table declares a column called ``rowID`` — the laboratory microplate row, ``'r1'``, ``'r2'`` — and SQLite identifiers are case-insensitive, so a bare ``rowid`` resolves to *that column* rather than to the row id. On a measurements database, ``max(rowid)`` scans the whole table to take the maximum of a text column (measured: 21 ms warm, 41 ms cold, on a 200 000-row table, the ``COUNT(*)`` cost this method avoids), and ``int('r16')`` then raises ``ValueError``, which is not a ``sqlite3.Error`` and would escape the caller's handler into the Qt event loop. :mod:`spacr.predictions`, :mod:`spacr.foreign` and :mod:`spacr.data_manager` handle the same shadowing.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.column_picker.SchemaReader.estimate_rows#2

records.source: It is spelt ``_rowid_`` for a reason. On a measurements database, ``max(rowid)`` scans the whole table to take the maximum of a text column (measured: 21 ms warm, 41 ms cold, on a 200 000-row table, the ``COUNT(*)`` cost this method avoids), and ``int('r16')`` then raises ``ValueError``, which is not a ``sqlite3.Error`` and would escape the caller's handler into the Qt event loop. :mod:`spacr.predictions`, :mod:`spacr.foreign` and :mod:`spacr.data_manager` handle the same shadowing.
records.translation: इसे ``_rowid_`` लिखने का कारण है। spaCR की हर object तालिका ``rowID`` नाम का कॉलम घोषित करती है — प्लेट की पंक्ति, ``'r1'``, ``'r2'`` — और SQLite identifiers case-insensitive हैं, इसलिए साधारण ``rowid`` row id के बजाय *उस कॉलम* में निर्धारित होता है। measurements डेटाबेस पर ``max(rowid)`` एक text कॉलम का अधिकतम लेने के लिए पूरी तालिका scan करता है (मापा गया: 200 000-पंक्ति तालिका पर 21 ms warm, 41 ms cold, यानी वही ``COUNT(*)`` लागत जिससे यह method बचता है), और फिर ``int('r16')`` ``ValueError`` उठाता है, जो ``sqlite3.Error`` नहीं है और कॉलर के handler से निकलकर Qt event loop में पहुँच जाएगा। :mod:`spacr.predictions`, :mod:`spacr.foreign` और :mod:`spacr.data_manager` भी यही छायांकन सँभालते हैं।

records.source: A screening campaign is dozens of plates run over weeks. Hit calling, plate normalisation and Z' all assume that the positive and negative controls behave the same way on every plate. When the controls drift — the cell line changes, a reagent lot changes, incubation conditions change — every downstream result shifts with them, and the analysis does not detect it, because it normalises to the controls it is given.
records.translation: स्क्रीनिंग अभियान दर्जनों प्लेटें हैं जो हफ़्तों में चलाई जाती हैं। hit calling, प्लेट normalisation और Z' सभी यह मानते हैं कि positive और negative controls हर प्लेट पर एक जैसा व्यवहार करते हैं। जब controls खिसकते हैं — cell line बदलती है, reagent lot बदलता है, incubation की स्थितियाँ बदलती हैं — तो हर बाद का परिणाम उनके साथ खिसक जाता है, और विश्लेषण इसे नहीं पकड़ता, क्योंकि वह उन्हीं controls के सापेक्ष normalise करता है जो उसे दिए गए हैं।

records.context: :data:`ESTIMATOR_MOVING_RANGE` Individuals / moving range (I-MR). One control value per laboratory microplate is the normal case in a screen, so this is what :data:`ESTIMATOR_AUTO` picks when every laboratory microplate contributes a single control microplate sample position. Sigma is ``mean(|x_i - x_{i-1}|) / 1.128``; 1.128 is d2 for a subgroup of two, which is what a moving range of consecutive points is.

records.source: :data:`ESTIMATOR_MOVING_RANGE` Individuals / moving range (I-MR). One control value per plate is the normal case in a screen, so this is what :data:`ESTIMATOR_AUTO` picks when every plate contributes a single control well. Sigma is ``mean(|x_i - x_{i-1}|) / 1.128``; 1.128 is d2 for a subgroup of two, which is what a moving range of consecutive points is.
records.translation: :data:`ESTIMATOR_MOVING_RANGE` Individuals / moving range (I-MR)। स्क्रीनिंग में प्रति प्लेट एक control मान सामान्य स्थिति है, इसलिए जब हर प्लेट एक ही control well देती है तो :data:`ESTIMATOR_AUTO` यही चुनता है। Sigma ``mean(|x_i - x_{i-1}|) / 1.128`` है; 1.128 दो के subgroup के लिए d2 है, और लगातार बिंदुओं की moving range यही होती है।

records.context: :data:`ESTIMATOR_SUBGROUP_S` X-bar / S, for a laboratory microplate with several control microplate sample positions (subgroup ``n > 1``). The plotted point is the laboratory microplate's mean and sigma is ``S-bar / c4(n)``, where :func:`c4` is computed from the gamma function rather than looked up in a table. The published table stops at n = 25, does not interpolate, and is prone to transcription errors. ``c4(n) = sqrt(2/(n-1)) · Γ(n/2) / Γ((n-1)/2)`` is three lines, is exact for every n, and can be checked against the published constant — ``c4(5) = 0.9400`` — which is what the test does.

records.context: The two robust constants are *not* interchangeable, and the module keeps them separate. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) is ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, the factor that makes the MAD of a normal sample an unbiased estimate of its SD. A moving range is ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, the absolute value of a *difference* of two observations, so its scale is ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` and its median is ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplying a median moving range by 1.4826 overestimates sigma by exactly ``sqrt(2)``, which makes the limits 41% wider and can hide a drift. Both constants are computed from ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` here for the same reason c4 is computed from the gamma function.

records.translation: दोनों robust स्थिरांक परस्पर विनिमेय *नहीं* हैं, और मॉड्यूल उन्हें अलग रखता है। 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` है, वह गुणक जो normal नमूने के MAD को उसके SD का निष्पक्ष आकलन बनाता है। moving range ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|`` है, दो प्रेक्षणों के *अंतर* का निरपेक्ष मान, इसलिए उसका scale ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` है और उसका median ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`)। median moving range को 1.4826 से गुणा करने पर sigma ठीक ``sqrt(2)`` गुना अधिक आँका जाता है, जिससे सीमाएँ 41% चौड़ी हो जाती हैं और drift छिप सकता है। दोनों स्थिरांक यहाँ ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` से गणना किए जाते हैं, उसी कारण से जिससे c4 gamma फ़ंक्शन से गणना किया जाता है।

records.context: **Limits estimated from an out-of-control baseline are unreliable.** When the baseline itself contains a violation, :meth:`ControlChartResult.caveats` says so. Re-estimating without the flagged plates is *offered* (:attr:`ControlChartSpec.reestimate`) and is off by default, so plates are never removed from the baseline without the user asking. It runs one pass, not iterations to convergence: iterating shrinks the limits onto the tightest subset of the baseline and eventually flags everything.

records.context: Which points a rule flags is a convention, and an unstated one makes two implementations disagree about the same chart, so it is stated: **every point that is part of the evidence is flagged.** For rule 1 that is the point itself. For the run rules (2, 3, 4, 7, 8) it is every point of the run, reported as one maximal span rather than as a sliding window's worth of overlapping alarms — which is what lets :meth:`ControlChartResult.report` say "laboratory microplates P22–P30 are nine in a row above the centre line" instead of listing three violations. For the "k of m" rules (5, 6) it is the qualifying points only: a window can trigger on two points beyond 2 sigma with a third sitting on the centre line, and that third point is not flagged because it is not part of the evidence.

records.context: The rule set is selectable, and it has to be, because **running all eight is not eight times the sensitivity**. Each rule has its own in-control false-alarm rate; :data:`RULE_ALARM_RATE` carries them, :meth:`ControlChartResult.caveats` does the arithmetic for the set that actually ran, and over a 200-plate campaign it reports the expected number of false alarms. :data:`RULES_DEFAULT` is the Western Electric four (1, 2, 5, 6), which is the set the classical ARL figure was worked out for; :data:`RULES_ALL` is all eight, and :data:`RULES_LIMITS_ONLY` is rule 1 alone for a user who wants limits and nothing else.

records.source: "Plate by plate over time" means the x axis is **run order**, and rules 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8 are statements about a sequence, so they are meaningless when the order is wrong. An explicit order or date column (:attr:`ControlChartSpec.order`) is used when given. Without one the plate id is sorted with a natural, digit-aware key so plate 2 comes before plate 10, and :attr:`ControlChartResult.order_inferred` is set, the note is in :attr:`ControlChartResult.notes`, and :meth:`ControlChartResult.report` says it in capitals.
records.translation: "समय के साथ प्लेट-दर-प्लेट" का अर्थ है कि x अक्ष **run क्रम** है, और नियम 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 और 8 किसी अनुक्रम के बारे में कथन हैं, इसलिए क्रम गलत होने पर वे अर्थहीन हैं। स्पष्ट order या date कॉलम (:attr:`ControlChartSpec.order`) दिए जाने पर उपयोग होता है। उसके बिना प्लेट id को प्राकृतिक, अंक-सजग कुंजी से छाँटा जाता है ताकि प्लेट 2 प्लेट 10 से पहले आए, और :attr:`ControlChartResult.order_inferred` सेट होता है, टिप्पणी :attr:`ControlChartResult.notes` में होती है, और :meth:`ControlChartResult.report` इसे बड़े अक्षरों में कहता है।

records.context: The key is a deliberate extension of :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec._sort_key`, not a copy of it: that one tries ``float(text)`` and falls back to a plain string compare, which puts ``P10`` before ``P2`` — fine for facet labels, wrong for a run order. Here the string is split into digit and non-digit runs and the digit runs compare as integers.

records.context: That asymmetry is the reason short-term (within-subgroup) variation is the only admissible sigma for a control chart, and it is pinned by a test. What the SD route *would* have said is computed anyway and reported — see :func:`sd_reference_limits` and :attr:`ControlChartResult.sd_would_flag` — so the two sets of limits can be compared directly.

records.context: The casing is load-bearing; the orientation is what makes it part of the rain. It used to be stored as a single token in a single cell and drawn horizontally, overflowing rightwards across its neighbours — which read as a label pasted over the effect rather than as part of it, and cost the renderer a whole second paint pass, measured token widths, widened dirty rectangles and a cleared backing rectangle so neighbouring glyphs did not tangle with the letters. None of that machinery exists now: every cell holds exactly one character, so the word is cached and blitted like any other glyph and cannot overdraw anything. See :data:`SPACR_SPLICE_PROBABILITY` for the rate and what it works out to in practice.

It used to be stored as a single token in a single cell and drawn horizontally, overflowing rightwards across its neighbours — which read as a label pasted over the effect rather than as part of it, and cost the renderer a whole second paint pass, measured token widths, widened dirty rectangles and a cleared backing rectangle so neighbouring glyphs did not tangle with the letters. None of that machinery exists now: every cell holds exactly one character, so the word is cached and blitted like any other glyph and cannot overdraw anything. See :data:`SPACR_SPLICE_PROBABILITY` for the rate and what it works out to in practice.
records.translation: अक्षरों का case महत्वपूर्ण है; दिशा ही इसे वर्षा का हिस्सा बनाती है। पहले इसे एक cell में एक token के रूप में रखा जाता था और क्षैतिज रूप से बनाया जाता था, जो दाईं ओर पड़ोसियों के ऊपर फैल जाता था — जो प्रभाव का हिस्सा होने के बजाय उसके ऊपर चिपकाए गए label जैसा दिखता था, और renderer को इसके लिए पूरा दूसरा paint pass, मापी गई token चौड़ाइयाँ, चौड़े किए गए dirty आयत और एक साफ़ किया गया backing आयत चाहिए होता था ताकि पड़ोसी glyphs अक्षरों से न उलझें। उस तंत्र में से अब कुछ भी (None) मौजूद नहीं है: हर cell में ठीक एक अक्षर होता है, इसलिए शब्द किसी भी अन्य glyph की तरह कैश और blit होता है और किसी चीज़ के ऊपर नहीं बन सकता। दर और व्यवहार में उसके परिणाम के लिए :data:`SPACR_SPLICE_PROBABILITY` देखें।

records.source: This runs behind the sequencing pipeline, so it has to be close to free. Three things get it there, and all three were measured rather than assumed (1920x1080, 120 columns, 67 rows):
records.translation: यह sequencing pipeline के पीछे चलता है, इसलिए इसे लगभग मुफ़्त होना चाहिए। तीन चीज़ें इसे वहाँ तक पहुँचाती हैं, और तीनों मानी नहीं गईं बल्कि मापी गईं (1920x1080, 120 कॉलम, 67 पंक्तियाँ):

records.context: 1. *The timer stops whenever the widget is not on application view* — hidden, or in a minimised window. Zero frames, zero CPU. 2. *Each string is pre-rendered once into an opaque pixmap* with the background already composited in, and blitted at its current offset every frame. Drawing 5400 glyphs with ``drawText`` costs 35 ms a frame; the same glyphs as 120 opaque strips cost 0.46 ms — and an opaque strip is 25x cheaper to blit than a translucent one, which is why the alpha is baked in rather than applied by the painter. A strip is re-rendered only when its column respawns or the styling changes; the cache is ~7 MB at 1920x1080. :meth:`DnaRainWidget.set_backdrop` gives that up deliberately — a picture under the rain is not a constant to bake against — so the translucent path is taken only by the themes that have a wallpaper to show, and dark and light keep the numbers above. 3. *Only the columns that moved are repainted.* Positions are quantised to whole cells, so a column is dirty only when its integer row changes — slow columns cost nothing on most ticks. See :data:`MAX_DIRTY_RECTS` for where partial repaints stop paying.

A strip is re-rendered only when its column respawns or the styling changes; the cache is ~7 MB at 1920x1080. :meth:`DnaRainWidget.set_backdrop` gives that up deliberately — a picture under the rain is not a constant to bake against — so the translucent path is taken only by the themes that have a wallpaper to show, and dark and light keep the numbers above. 3. *Only the columns that moved are repainted.* Positions are quantised to whole cells, so a column is dirty only when its integer row changes — slow columns cost nothing on most ticks. See :data:`MAX_DIRTY_RECTS` for where partial repaints stop paying.
records.translation: 1. *विजेट के स्क्रीन पर न होने पर timer रुक जाता है* — छिपा हो, या minimise की गई विंडो में हो। शून्य frames, शून्य CPU। 2. *हर string एक बार एक अपारदर्शी pixmap में पहले से render की जाती है*, जिसमें पृष्ठभूमि पहले से composite होती है, और हर frame में अपने वर्तमान offset पर blit की जाती है। ``drawText`` से 5400 glyphs बनाने में प्रति frame 35 ms लगते हैं; वही glyphs 120 अपारदर्शी पट्टियों के रूप में 0.46 ms लेते हैं — और अपारदर्शी पट्टी को blit करना पारभासी पट्टी से 25x सस्ता है, इसी कारण alpha को painter से लागू करने के बजाय पहले से शामिल किया जाता है। पट्टी केवल तब फिर से render होती है जब उसका कॉलम respawn होता है या styling बदलती है; 1920x1080 पर cache ~7 MB है। :meth:`DnaRainWidget.set_backdrop` इसे जानबूझकर छोड़ देता है — वर्षा के नीचे का चित्र कोई स्थिरांक नहीं जिसके सापेक्ष पहले से render किया जाए — इसलिए पारभासी पथ केवल उन थीमों द्वारा लिया जाता है जिनके पास दिखाने को wallpaper है, और dark तथा light ऊपर की संख्याएँ बनाए रखती हैं। 3. *केवल हिले हुए कॉलम फिर से चित्रित होते हैं।* स्थितियाँ पूरे cells पर quantise की जाती हैं, इसलिए कॉलम केवल तब dirty होता है जब उसकी पूर्णांक पंक्ति बदलती है — धीमे कॉलम अधिकांश ticks पर कुछ नहीं लेते। आंशिक repaint कहाँ लाभकारी नहीं रहते, इसके लिए :data:`MAX_DIRTY_RECTS` देखें।

records.context: The rain is an opaque backdrop by construction — it repaints only the cells that changed, so it has to be able to *clear* them, and clearing to a translucent colour smears the previous frame. That is the right trade on the dark and light themes, where the thing behind it is a flat ``bg`` the rain can reproduce exactly. On an image theme it is not: the flat colour is nothing like the wallpaper, and an opaque rain hid the photograph completely on the one application view that has a rain.

records.source: The rain is an opaque backdrop by construction — it repaints only the cells that changed, so it has to be able to *clear* them, and clearing to a translucent colour smears the previous frame. That is the right trade on the dark and light themes, where the thing behind it is a flat ``bg`` the rain can reproduce exactly. On an image theme it is not: the flat colour is nothing like the wallpaper, and an opaque rain hid the photograph completely on the one screen that has a rain.
records.translation: rain अपनी बनावट से ही एक अपारदर्शी पृष्ठभूमि है — यह केवल बदले हुए cells को repaint करता है, इसलिए इसे उन्हें *साफ़* करने में सक्षम होना चाहिए, और पारभासी रंग से साफ़ करने पर पिछला frame धुँधला फैल जाता है। dark और light थीमों पर यह सही समझौता है, जहाँ पीछे की चीज़ एक समतल ``bg`` है जिसे rain ठीक-ठीक दोहरा सकता है। image थीम पर ऐसा नहीं है: समतल रंग wallpaper जैसा बिल्कुल नहीं है, और अपारदर्शी rain ने उस एकमात्र स्क्रीन पर फ़ोटो को पूरी तरह छिपा दिया जिसमें rain है।

records.context: Handing the wallpaper in fixes that without giving up the dirty-rectangle repaint: the clear becomes a blit of the corresponding piece of the image, aligned to where the window's own stylesheet paints it, and the strips switch to per-pixel alpha so the glyphs composite over the picture instead of over a colour baked into them.

records.translation: wallpaper देने से dirty-rectangle repaint छोड़े बिना यह ठीक हो जाता है: साफ़ करना छवि के संबंधित हिस्से का blit बन जाता है, जो उसी जगह संरेखित होता है जहाँ विंडो की अपनी stylesheet उसे चित्रित करती है, और पट्टियाँ प्रति-pixel alpha पर चली जाती हैं ताकि glyphs अपने भीतर पहले से शामिल रंग के बजाय चित्र के ऊपर composite हों।

records.context: Deliberately does NOT consult `population()`. Hit-testing a data-selection boundary is pure geometry -- is this coordinate inside this shape -- and needs no rows at all. Asking for the population first meant that whenever it was unavailable, dragging died silently: `population()` returns None when the active data-selection boundary no longer exists, which is exactly the state left behind by DELETING a data-selection boundary. The remaining data-selection boundary then looked "fixed and I cannot move".

records.source: Deliberately does NOT consult `population()`. Hit-testing a gate is pure geometry -- is this coordinate inside this shape -- and needs no rows at all. Asking for the population first meant that whenever it was unavailable, dragging died silently: `population()` returns None when the active gate no longer exists, which is exactly the state left behind by DELETING a gate. The remaining gate then looked "fixed and I cannot move".
records.translation: जानबूझकर `population()` से परामर्श नहीं (NOT) करता। gate का hit-testing शुद्ध ज्यामिति है -- क्या यह निर्देशांक इस आकृति के भीतर है -- और इसे किसी पंक्ति की आवश्यकता नहीं। पहले population माँगने का अर्थ था कि जब भी वह अनुपलब्ध होती, खींचना चुपचाप बंद हो जाता: सक्रिय gate के अब मौजूद न होने पर `population()` None लौटाता है, और gate हटाने (DELETING) के बाद ठीक यही स्थिति बचती है। तब बचा हुआ gate "स्थिर, और मैं हिला नहीं सकता" जैसा दिखता था।

records.context: **The asymmetry problem is real and is not fixed by choosing a bigger c.** Tukey's fence is symmetric in the quartiles, and a right-skewed distribution therefore has far more mass beyond the upper fence than beyond the lower one *by construction*, whatever the data. For a lognormal with sigma = 1 the standard fence flags about 8% of the sample on the right and essentially nothing on the left — and it does so for a perfectly clean sample. Read uncorrected, "8% of my cells are outliers" is a statement about the shape of the distribution, not about the cells.

records.source: **The asymmetry problem is real and is not fixed by choosing a bigger c.** Tukey's fence is symmetric in the quartiles, and a right-skewed distribution therefore has far more mass beyond the upper fence than beyond the lower one *by construction*, whatever the data. For a lognormal with sigma = 1 the standard fence flags about 8% of the sample on the right and essentially nothing on the left — and it does so for a perfectly clean sample. Read uncorrected, "8% of my cells are outliers" is a statement about the shape of the distribution, not about the cells.
records.translation: **विषमता की समस्या वास्तविक है और बड़ा c चुनने से ठीक नहीं होती।** Tukey's fence quartiles में सममित है, और इसलिए दाईं ओर विषम वितरण में ऊपरी fence के पार निचली की तुलना में *बनावट से ही* कहीं अधिक द्रव्यमान होता है, डेटा चाहे जो हो। sigma = 1 वाले lognormal के लिए मानक fence दाईं ओर नमूने का लगभग 8% चिह्नित करता है और बाईं ओर लगभग कुछ नहीं — और पूरी तरह स्वच्छ नमूने पर भी ऐसा करता है। बिना सुधार के पढ़ा जाए तो "मेरी 8% कोशिकाएँ outliers हैं" वितरण के आकार के बारे में कथन है, कोशिकाओं के बारे में नहीं।

records.context: The offered remedy is a **log10 transform**, :data:`TRANSFORM_LOG10`, which turns a lognormal into a Gaussian and makes the fence mean what it appears to mean. It is **never implicit**: a transform silently applied would change what ``outlier_score`` is in units of without the user asking. And it **refuses** rather than fudges on non-positive values — ``log10`` of a zero ``pathogen_area`` is ``-inf``, and an implicit ``+1`` or a dropped row would be an invented measurement or a self-selected population. The refusal names the feature and the count.

records.context: **Why MCD and not an isolation forest.** Both are "multivariate outlier detectors" and they are not interchangeable:
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model#18
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Why MCD and not an isolation forest.** Both are "multivariate outlier detectors" and they are not interchangeable:
records.translation: **MCD क्यों, isolation forest क्यों नहीं।** दोनों "multivariate outlier detectors" हैं और वे परस्पर विनिमेय नहीं हैं:

records.context: **The threshold is a stated false-positive rate, not a tuned fraction.** Under multivariate normality the squared robust Mahalanobis distance is distributed chi-square with ``p`` degrees of freedom, so the cut point is ``chi2.ppf(1 - alpha, p)`` for a chosen ``alpha`` — default :data:`DEFAULT_ALPHA` = 0.001, meaning *one clean object in a thousand is expected to be flagged*. Over 10^5 objects that is about 100 false flags, and over the 200,000 objects of a typical two-plate screen it is about 200. That number is knowable in advance and is printed in :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats`. An isolation forest's score has no such null distribution and therefore no calibrated cut point at all.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model#19
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The threshold is a stated false-positive rate, not a tuned fraction.** Under multivariate normality the squared robust Mahalanobis distance is distributed chi-square with ``p`` degrees of freedom, so the cut point is ``chi2.ppf(1 - alpha, p)`` for a chosen ``alpha`` — default :data:`DEFAULT_ALPHA` = 0.001, meaning *one clean object in a thousand is expected to be flagged*. Over 10^5 objects that is about 100 false flags, and over the 200,000 objects of a typical two-plate screen it is about 200. That number is knowable in advance and is printed in :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats`. An isolation forest's score has no such null distribution and therefore no calibrated cut point at all.
records.translation: **threshold एक घोषित false-positive दर है, tune किया गया अंश नहीं।** multivariate normality के अंतर्गत squared robust Mahalanobis दूरी ``p`` degrees of freedom के chi-square के अनुसार वितरित होती है, इसलिए cut point ``chi2.ppf(1 - alpha, p)`` है, चुने गए ``alpha`` के लिए — डिफ़ॉल्ट :data:`DEFAULT_ALPHA` = 0.001, अर्थात *हज़ार में एक स्वच्छ object के चिह्नित होने की अपेक्षा है*। 10^5 objects पर यह लगभग 100 गलत चिह्न है, और सामान्य दो-प्लेट स्क्रीनिंग के 200,000 objects पर लगभग 200। यह संख्या पहले से जानी जा सकती है और :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats` में छापी जाती है। isolation forest के score का ऐसा कोई null वितरण नहीं है और इसलिए कोई calibrated cut point भी नहीं।

records.context: The obvious thing to write here is ``|x - mean| / sd > 3``, and it is the one thing this module refuses to do. spaCR object measurements are skewed and heavy-tailed by construction: ``cell_area`` is a positive quantity with a long right tail, ``pathogen_area`` is zero-inflated, an intensity ratio has a denominator that can approach zero. The mean and the SD of such a column are themselves dragged by the very objects they are supposed to find — one debris particle measured at 40× the median area moves the mean, inflates the SD, and so raises the threshold that was meant to catch it. The failure is silent and it gets worse the worse the contamination is: this is the *masking* effect, and it is the reason robust statistics exist.

records.source: The obvious thing to write here is ``|x - mean| / sd > 3``, and it is the one thing this module refuses to do. spaCR object measurements are skewed and heavy-tailed by construction: ``cell_area`` is a positive quantity with a long right tail, ``pathogen_area`` is zero-inflated, an intensity ratio has a denominator that can approach zero. The failure is silent and it gets worse the worse the contamination is: this is the *masking* effect, and it is the reason robust statistics exist.
records.translation: यहाँ लिखने के लिए स्पष्ट चीज़ ``|x - mean| / sd > 3`` है, और यही वह एक चीज़ है जिसे यह मॉड्यूल करने से मना करता है। spaCR object measurements अपनी बनावट से ही विषम और भारी-पूँछ वाले होते हैं: ``cell_area`` लंबी दाईं पूँछ वाली धनात्मक मात्रा है, ``pathogen_area`` zero-inflated है, intensity अनुपात का हर शून्य के निकट जा सकता है। ऐसे कॉलम का mean और SD स्वयं उन्हीं objects से खिंच जाते हैं जिन्हें उन्हें खोजना है — median क्षेत्रफल के 40× मापा गया एक debris कण mean को खिसका देता है, SD को फुला देता है, और इस तरह उसी threshold को ऊँचा कर देता है जिसे उसे पकड़ना था। विफलता चुपचाप होती है और संदूषण जितना बुरा हो उतनी ही बुरी होती जाती है: यही *masking* प्रभाव है, और robust statistics के अस्तित्व का कारण यही है।

records.context: **MCD is affine-equivariant.** Rescale ``area`` from px^2 to um^2, or rotate to any linear combination of the features, and the fitted centre and covariance transform with it: every distance, and so every flag, is unchanged. This is the same invariance argument :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model` makes for standardising before a PCA, and it is why no scaling option is needed here — the metric *is* the covariance. A tree ensemble splits on raw coordinates and is not equivariant; its answer depends on the units.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model#21

records.source: **MCD is affine-equivariant.** Rescale ``area`` from px^2 to um^2, or rotate to any linear combination of the features, and the fitted centre and covariance transform with it: every distance, and so every flag, is unchanged. This is the same invariance argument :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model` makes for standardising before a PCA, and it is why no scaling option is needed here — the metric *is* the covariance. A tree ensemble splits on raw coordinates and is not equivariant; its answer depends on the units.
records.translation: **MCD affine-equivariant है।** ``area`` को px^2 से um^2 में बदलें, या features के किसी भी रैखिक संयोजन में घुमाएँ, और fit किया गया केंद्र तथा covariance उसके साथ रूपांतरित होते हैं: हर दूरी, और इसलिए हर चिह्न, अपरिवर्तित रहता है। यह वही invariance तर्क है जो :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model` PCA से पहले standardise करने के लिए देता है, और इसी कारण यहाँ किसी scaling विकल्प की आवश्यकता नहीं — metric स्वयं covariance *है*। tree ensemble कच्चे निर्देशांकों पर विभाजन करता है और equivariant नहीं है; उसका उत्तर इकाइयों पर निर्भर करता है।

records.context: **MCD is the multivariate generalisation of the median and the MAD.** The MCD centre is a multivariate median (the mean of the h-subset of minimum covariance determinant) and the MCD scatter is its spread. So all three methods offered here are the same idea at one, one, and p dimensions, and a user who understands the MAD already understands this.

records.context: **The cost, stated.** MCD needs ``n > p`` to have a covariance at all, and it is unstable until roughly ``n >= 2p`` (:data:`MCD_MIN_OBJECTS_PER_FEATURE` * p): the estimate is fitted on a *subset* of about ``n/2`` rows, so ``n = 2p`` already means the subset is only barely larger than the dimension. records.context: **The 1.4826.** For a Gaussian, ``MAD = Phi^-1(0.75) * sigma = 0.6745 * sigma``, so ``sigma = MAD / 0.6745 = 1.4826 * MAD``. Multiplying by :data:`MAD_TO_SIGMA` makes the MAD a *consistent estimator of sigma* under normality, which is what lets the threshold be read on the familiar scale — "3.5 SD" — while never being computed from an SD that the outliers could inflate. The constant is the whole reason ``k`` is comparable to a z-score cut-off at all; without it, ``k`` would be in units of "MADs" and 3.5 would mean something different for every column.

records.translation: **1.4826।** Gaussian के लिए ``MAD = Phi^-1(0.75) * sigma = 0.6745 * sigma``, इसलिए ``sigma = MAD / 0.6745 = 1.4826 * MAD``। :data:`MAD_TO_SIGMA` से गुणा करने पर MAD normality के अंतर्गत *sigma का सुसंगत estimator* बन जाता है, जिससे threshold को परिचित पैमाने — "3.5 SD" — पर पढ़ा जा सकता है, जबकि वह कभी ऐसे SD से गणना नहीं होता जिसे outliers फुला सकें। यही स्थिरांक पूरा कारण है कि ``k`` की z-score cut-off से तुलना हो पाती है; इसके बिना ``k`` "MADs" की इकाइयों में होता और 3.5 का अर्थ हर कॉलम के लिए अलग होता।

records.context: **MAD == 0 is handled, not divided by.** When more than half the objects share one value — a zero-inflated ``pathogen_area``, an integer count, a saturated intensity — the MAD is exactly zero. Naively, every value that differs at all then scores infinity and *the entire tail is flagged*, which is the opposite of robust. So :func:`robust_scale` falls back to the **mean absolute deviation from the median**, scaled by :data:`MEAN_AD_TO_SIGMA` = ``sqrt(pi/2)`` = 1.2533 (for a Gaussian ``E|X - mu| = sigma * sqrt(2/pi)``), and says so in :attr:`OutlierResult.notes` and in :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats`.

records.context: The alternative considered and not taken is the Rousseeuw–Croux ``Sn`` (``1.1926 * med_i med_j |x_i - x_j|``), which is the statistically better answer: it has a 50% breakdown point, needs no symmetry assumption, and does not collapse on tied data. It is not used because the naive form is O(n^2) — unusable on the 10^5–10^6 object rows spaCR routinely produces — and the O(n log n) algorithm is a page of intricate code to maintain for a path that is only ever reached when the MAD has *already* collapsed. The mean absolute deviation has a 0% breakdown point and that is stated plainly rather than glossed: it is a stopgap that keeps a degenerate column from flagging its whole tail, not a robust estimator. If the fallback fires, the column is probably not continuous enough for this test.

records.translation: विचार किया गया पर न अपनाया गया विकल्प Rousseeuw–Croux ``Sn`` (``1.1926 * med_i med_j |x_i - x_j|``) है, जो सांख्यिकीय रूप से बेहतर उत्तर है: इसका breakdown point 50% है, इसे symmetry की धारणा नहीं चाहिए, और यह tied डेटा पर ढहता नहीं। इसका उपयोग इसलिए नहीं होता कि सीधा रूप O(n^2) है — spaCR द्वारा नियमित रूप से बनाई जाने वाली 10^5–10^6 object पंक्तियों पर अनुपयोगी — और O(n log n) algorithm ऐसे पथ के लिए रखरखाव हेतु एक पृष्ठ जटिल कोड है जो केवल तब पहुँचता है जब MAD *पहले ही* ढह चुका हो। mean absolute deviation का breakdown point 0% है और यह बात छिपाने के बजाय स्पष्ट कही जाती है: यह एक अस्थायी उपाय है जो किसी degenerate कॉलम को उसकी पूरी पूँछ चिह्नित करने से रोकता है, robust estimator नहीं। यदि fallback चलता है, तो कॉलम संभवतः इस परीक्षण के लिए पर्याप्त continuous नहीं है।

records.context: Filtering changes a Q-Q plot in a way it does not change a volcano. records.context: No statistic is recomputed here. The statistics come from :func:`spacr.regression_qc.draw_panel` -- Spearman's rho on sqrt|standardised residual| against fitted, a Brown-Forsythe test across quartiles of the fitted value, and the quartile SD ratio -- drawn into a throwaway axes purely to get the key-value mapping it returns.
